hero.title: Developing Mission-Aligned Revenue Streams
hero.subtitle: An overview of Roadrunner Food Bank's innovation and earned-revenue programming — who we are, why this matters, what we're building, and how to get involved.

whoWeAre.headline: Roadrunner Food Bank is New Mexico's food-access backbone
whoWeAre.mission: Provide nourishing food to New Mexicans through vibrant community partnerships and passionate public and private support.
facts: Founded in 1979; Roadrunner Food Bank (RRFB) is New Mexico's largest food non-profit dedicated to solving food insecurity and the only Feeding America member in the state.
400+ partner agencies spanning schools, shelters, churches, health clinics, senior centers, tribal entities, colleges, and community organizations.
80% of all food provided through partner agencies was procured, warehoused, and distributed by RRFB.
Access models include pantries, mobile distributions, SNAP and benefits support, home delivery, workforce training, Food Is Medicine, and refrigerated lockers.
whoWeAre.coreIdea: RRFB is not just a distributor — it is statewide infrastructure with trust, logistics, data, and community reach.

whyNow.headline: Rising need and constrained funding require a more resilient model
whyNow.sub: Innovation and earned revenue strengthen the mission; they do not replace philanthropy or public support.

reasons.title: Need is rising
reasons.body: Food insecurity in New Mexico and across the U.S. is rising at the same time as fuel and food costs are also increasing.
reasons.stat: 1 in 6 New Mexicans are food insecure

reasons.title: Traditional funding is not enough
reasons.body: Grants, philanthropy, and public funding remain essential. Additive revenue sources support long-term operating capacity and help expand infrastructure.
reasons.stat: 90%+ of RRFB current revenue is from contributions and grants

reasons.title: RRFB has underused capabilities
reasons.body: Borrowing practices from other segments, RRFB can package expertise, relationships, data, and operating infrastructure into marketable services and ventures.
reasons.stat: 100+ years of combined logistics, cross-border trade, and Food Is Medicine expertise

closing: The question we ask isn't “how do we raise more?”
It's “what can build and sustain RRFB's mission?”

portfolio.headline: Five program areas
portfolio.sub: Five lanes make up a practical, working portfolio: three earned-revenue verticals plus two lanes that make the other three possible.

items.name: FIM Advisory Services
items.description: Readiness assessments, training, implementation support, and pricing tests for community-based organizations and health-system partners.

items.name: Medically Tailored Meals
items.description: Assessing production and distribution, payer pathways, clinical partnership fit, unit economics, and what it would take to launch.

items.name: Waste-to-Value Solutions
items.description: Exploring biochar and other side-stream revenue opportunities linked to food waste and operations.

items.name: Research Programming
items.description: Standing up statements of work, subawards, data governance, evaluation budgets, and community-based research roles with academic partners.

items.name: FIM Innovation Pilots
items.description: Identifying right-sized software and technology to prepare community organizations for Medicaid reimbursement for Food Is Medicine.

vetting.eyebrow: How we choose what to pursue
vetting.headline: Selecting what fits the mission, the market, and the operating model
vetting.sub: The goal is disciplined innovation: advance work that can prove itself, and pause or stop ideas that lack demand, capacity, or capital fit.

criteria.name: Mission fit
criteria.description: Addresses food access, health, infrastructure, or waste — and strengthens RRFB's core role.

criteria.name: Demand fit
criteria.description: A funder, payer, partner, or customer has a clear reason to pay for the solution.

criteria.name: Operating fit
criteria.description: Uses RRFB capabilities without distracting from essential distribution work.

criteria.name: Financial fit
criteria.description: Can show pricing, cost, risk, and capital requirements before scaling.

selected: Opportunities with mission alignment and a real payment pathway
Work that can be piloted in 6–12 months
Projects with clear owners, partners, and evidence needs
Models that can become fundable, financeable, or generate recurring revenue

decisions.item: FIM technology pilots for reimbursement readiness
Medically tailored meals and waste-to-value concepts

vetting.rule: Our rule: scale what proves value; redesign or stop what does not.

items.title: Rural Health Innovation Fund proposal
items.description: Packages Medicaid-readiness and Food Is Medicine implementation support into a fundable, statewide CBO readiness model.

items.title: Southern New Mexico partner support
items.description: Translates Southern New Mexico access needs into lockers, route delivery, startup operations, project tracking, and outcomes reporting.

items.title: FIM advisory partnership with Luminar Health
items.description: Testing whether RRFB can package FIM reimbursement expertise into repeatable assessments, training, and implementation support with high statewide CBO demand.

roadmap.headline: The next three years take us from proof to a scale-ready portfolio
roadmap.closing: Scale what proves value; stop or restructure what does not.

stages.label: Year 1
stages.name: Prove
stages.description: Validate demand, pricing, delivery model, and unit economics. Convert the strongest opportunities into paying or funded work.

stages.label: 24 months
stages.name: Scale
stages.description: Expand proven service lines, build recurring customer relationships, and develop shared operating infrastructure.

stages.label: Year 3
stages.name: Ready to grow
stages.description: Operate a diversified portfolio with clear governance, staffing, capital needs, and pathways for rapid expansion.
